trust.commands.note: Its commands run only when you pick one.
trust.commands.title: Repository commands
trust.follows.note: What these hooks and settings run changes with the branch ({path} is in the working tree): Glowfly asks again before a checkout, merge, pull or rebase brings in other versions of it.
trust.forgot: Forgot the trust decision for {name}. Glowfly asks again the next time you open it.
trust.forgot_missing.one: Forgot the trust decision for {count} missing folder.
trust.forgot_missing.other: Forgot the trust decisions for {count} missing folders.
trust.forgot_with.one: Forgot the trust decision for {name} and the repository passed on from it.
trust.forgot_with.other: Forgot the trust decision for {name} and the {count} repositories passed on from it.
trust.gained.intro: These settings, hooks or commands that run programs appeared or changed since you trusted it. So far Glowfly has only read its files.
trust.halt.changed: a command before it changed the repository's settings or hooks
trust.halt.held: it brings other versions of {places}, which you haven't trusted
trust.halt.stopped: Glowfly stopped the job before its next command: {why}. Review the repository's trust, then run it again.
trust.incoming.intro: The commit this brings in has other versions of the hooks, scripts or settings files that change with the branch, and Git would run or read them during the command. So far Glowfly has only read them.
trust.incoming.title: Trust the incoming hooks and scripts?
trust.known.lfs.tip: Git LFS's standard setup: it runs the git-lfs installed on this computer, not a file from the repository.
trust.network.note: These can turn off certificate checks, send Git's traffic, sign-ins included, through another server, or name a file Git reads cookies from and writes them to.
trust.network.title: Settings that change how Git connects
trust.revoked: Revoked trust in {name}. Glowfly asks again before Git runs its settings or hooks.
trust.revoked_with.one: Revoked trust in {name} and the repository passed on from it. Glowfly asks again before Git runs their settings or hooks.
trust.revoked_with.other: Revoked trust in {name} and the {count} repositories passed on from it. Glowfly asks again before Git runs their settings or hooks.
trust.stale.held: {label} didn't start: the repository's settings or hooks changed since they were checked. Decide whether to trust them first.
trust.steps.note: Continuing or skipping in the rebase, cherry-pick or revert in progress runs these.
trust.steps.title: Commands the operation in progress runs
trust.unchecked.conflicted: Merging what it brings in would conflict in {path}, where hooks run from, leaving conflict markers in a hook. Trust and run runs it anyway.
trust.unchecked.patched: A patch it applies writes {path}, where hooks run from, and Git would run what it writes. Trust and run runs it anyway.
trust.unchecked.unmodeled: Glowfly can't tell what {what} writes where hooks run from, so it wasn't compared with what you trusted. Trust and run runs it anyway.
trust.unchecked.unreadable: Glowfly couldn't read the commits it brings in ({error}), as happens in a partial clone, so their hooks weren't compared with what you trusted. Trust and run runs it anyway; or fetch them first with hooks turned off (git -c core.hooksPath= fetch).
trust.unchecked.unresolved: Glowfly can't tell which commit {rev} names the way Git would, so the hooks it brings in weren't compared with what you trusted. Trust and run runs it anyway.
trust.unknown.name: Not recognised
trust.unknown.tip: Glowfly doesn't recognise this. Git would run it with your account's permissions.
